title: Local AI on Surface Laptop Ultra

slides.title: Local AI Architecture
slides.subtitle: Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark

slides.title: Hardware Layers
slides.notes: Surface Laptop Ultra features 20 CPU cores, 128 GB RAM (64 GB visible to OS), and an NVIDIA RTX Spark GPU. The GPU memory is 64,000 MiB as reported by nvidia-smi. This stack supports local AI workloads without cloud dependencies.

slides.title: Memory Views
slides.takeaway: RAM and GPU memory are separate
slides.notes: System RAM (64 GB visible) and GPU memory (64,000 MiB) are separate. Never combine them. Think of system RAM as office desks and GPU memory as specialized workstations. Each has its own allocation.

slides.title: Local AI Runtimes
slides.notes: The device runs local AI via llama.cpp (ARM64 CUDA build 11573) and Foundry Local with CUDA execution provider. These runtimes support native ARM64 execution for efficient model serving.

slides.title: Model Catalog
slides.notes: The device hosts 28 open models, totaling 315 GiB on disk. These models are used for code generation and internal RAG tasks.

slides.title: Model Throughput
slides.notes: Throughput varies by model and stream count. Qwen3-Coder 30B delivers 140 tokens/s across 4 streams, while Gemma 4 26B achieves 245 tokens/s across 8 streams. MoE models decode faster due to expert activation.

slides.title: MoE vs Dense Models

data.verdict: MoE models are faster for decoding

slides.notes: MoE models activate only a few experts per token, decoding faster than dense models of similar size. Dense models use all parameters, making them slower for decoding.

slides.title: Model Sizing Bands
slides.notes: Model sizing bands help estimate performance. S (1-4B), M (7-8B), L (14-20B), XL (24-32B) are planning estimates, not accuracy tiers.

slides.title: Local AI Use Cases
slides.notes: Local AI supports code generation and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over internal engineering documents. Tasks are kept local for IP safety.

slides.title: Hybrid Routing
slides.notes: Hybrid routing sends sensitive, frequent tasks (code, internal docs) to the local lane. Heaviest reasoning tasks route to cloud models. This balances performance and security.

slides.title: Made on Device
slides.notes: This deck was generated on the Surface Laptop Ultra by Qwen3-Coder 30B through llama.cpp, with no cloud calls. The device demonstrates its own local AI capabilities.

slides.title: Pilot Ask
slides.notes: Zava invites 10 developers for a 2-week pilot testing the local AI stack. The goal is to measure acceptance rate, latency, and developer experience. Feedback will inform future adoption.
